title: Ordering-equivalence and cross-language suite
purpose: Prove that equivalent plan representations produce one canonical body and digest and one decode outcome, that the declared per-collection ordering and duplicate-free activationOrder rules hold, and that diagnostics are ordered deterministically; provide the Python cross-language leg (compiler versus validator).
outputs: canonical plan bytes and domain-separated digests
state: static-immutable test source; decoded value plan-scoped
errors: assertion failure on an unexpected outcome, code, canonical byte, or digest

unit_cases.precondition: two synthetic plan bodies differing only in member order/whitespace
unit_cases.stimulus: canonicalize both with the T019 decoder

unit_cases.precondition: a dump(3) re-serialization of the committed T017 fixture
unit_cases.stimulus: decode and recompute the canonical body/digest
unit_cases.expected: same canonical bytes and recomputed digest as the original (T20-ORD-02)

unit_cases.precondition: a committed fixture with each identity-bearing collection in declared key order
unit_cases.expected: baseline accepted; reversed collection rejected XCOM-DECODE-SHAPE with no plan (T20-ORD-03)

unit_cases.stimulus: duplicate an entry, empty it, and reorder it completely
unit_cases.expected: duplicate/empty rejected XCOM-DECODE-SHAPE; complete reordered sequence accepted and preserved verbatim (T20-ORD-04)

unit_cases.stimulus: decode the fixture and equivalent representations
unit_cases.expected: decoded diagnostics equal the declared order and are identical across representations (T20-ORD-05)

unit_cases.precondition: the fixture and a reordered-but-equivalent document
unit_cases.expected: identical outcome, code, digest value/algorithm, and the compared decoded fields (T20-ORD-06, T20-DET-01, T20-DET-02)

unit_cases.precondition: a body with an integral token 100
unit_cases.expected: same canonical body and digest; still accepted (T20-ORD-07, T20-DET-03)

unit_cases.stimulus: decode repeatedly and hash with the domain separator
unit_cases.expected: identical outcome/code/digest; domain-separated SHA-256 deterministic (T20-ORD-08, T20-DET-01, T20-DET-04)

static_checks.rule: cppcheck --error-exitcode=1 --quiet --std=c++20 --language=c++ --suppress=invalidLifetime src/xverse/xcom/src/activation_plan.cpp reports no error/portability defect in the consumed T019 decoder source built into the T020 suites

static_checks.tool: GNU g++ 11.4.0 via CMake target xverse_xcom_activation_plan_t020_<kind>_tests with xverse_xcom_apply_warnings
static_checks.rule: the T020 test target compiles under the project strict warning flags with no warning and no error

note: The Python cases are executed by the trusted validation (pytest) measure and are not CTest-discovered, so they are not listed as unit-measure cases.
